flagged.evidence: Step 3.1 says, “After padding the finitely many coordinates used on each band into one fixed Euclidean space R^Q,” the two infinite sums are R^Q-valued. Step 2.1 supplies blocks H_m in R^{Q_m}, while cited shrinking lemma only supplies a countable locally finite family; it gives no uniform bound on the finite numbers Q_m. Thus finite-dimensional padding into one fixed Q is not licensed, and the asserted bounded finite-dimensional G is not constructed.

The statement takes an arbitrary compact subset K of M and calls F:K×B→N “a smooth family,” then speaks of its differential and a submersion along K×{0}. The cited definition says, “Let M, S, and N be smooth manifolds. A smooth family ... is a smooth map F:M×S→N.” An arbitrary compact K need not be a manifold (for example, it may be a Cantor set), so smoothness, the differential, and submersion are undefined here.

[L1] says the cited ambient tubular theorem gives the target N “a tubular neighbourhood in some ambient Euclidean space,” and step 1.1 says “Use [L1] to embed N as a closed submanifold of some R^m.” The cited theorem instead begins “Let i:S→M be a closed smooth embedded submanifold. Then S has a tubular neighbourhood in M”; it presupposes an ambient embedding and does not produce j:N→R^m. No Euclidean-embedding result is cited in this item.

Step 4.1 concludes that two preimages in possibly different W_i and W_j “lie in the same local branch” because E|_{W_i} is a diffeomorphism and E(W_i) meets the zero section only over U_i. These facts only give inverses on each individual image E(W_i); they do not imply E^{-1}(E(W_i))=W_i or exclude another preimage in W_j. The purported “nearest zero section point” is neither defined nor established. Hence global injectivity on Ω_delta does not follow.

Step 2.1 infers that the restriction is “a local diffeomorphism at every point of its domain” from [L1], which states only that normal addition is a local diffeomorphism “along the zero section.” Restricting the domain does not make the derivative invertible at nonzero normal vectors. No radius was chosen to preserve local-diffeomorphism points, so openness of the image and the claimed diffeomorphism are unproved.

Step 1.1 applies [L2] to “F|_V on the closed neighbourhood overline V,” although it has only arranged that F is smooth on the open set V. The cited extension lemma requires a closed C contained in an open U on which the input is smooth. In general overline V is not contained in V, and F|_V is not a smooth map on a neighbourhood of overline V. The needed additional nesting inside the original smooth neighbourhood is absent.

Step 2.1 assumes N>2n and then states that S^{N-1} has dimension N-1>2n. For the decisive case N=2n+1, however, N-1=2n. The cited lower-dimensional-image proposition requires strict inequality of dimensions, so it cannot show that tau_f(TM\setminus0_M) is null in that case. Step 4.1 nevertheless repeats this invalid reduction down to 2n.

Step 1.1 forms “a finite-dimensional perturbation family F^(r):K_r×B_r→N” from an unspecified compact exhaustion. As in its cited lemma, K_r is only a compact set, not a smooth manifold. The cited definition of smooth families requires a product of smooth manifolds, and the cited parametric transversality theorem likewise starts with a smooth family M×S→N. Thus the family, transversality, and slices used here are not defined.

Step 2.1 says one may choose generic parameters so that g_r is transverse on K_r “and agrees with g_{r-1} on a neighbourhood of K_{r-1}.” The families supplied in step 1.1 have zero slice f|_{K_r}; neither [L1] nor parametric transversality supplies a family based at g_{r-1}, supported away from K_{r-1}, or any overlap-patching data. Smallness of a_r cannot imply exact agreement on a neighbourhood.

After step 3.1 establishes only local diffeomorphisms near zero vectors, step 4.1 says to “shrink the domain by a positive smooth radius exactly as in the Euclidean normal-addition argument” and thereby obtain injectivity. [L3] supplies the Euclidean tubular theorem and the inverse function theorem, not a theorem that an arbitrary map locally diffeomorphic along a zero section has a globally injective variable-radius restriction. The required global branch-separation argument is not provided.

Step 1.1 claims that a basic strong neighbourhood is determined by “finitely many compact sets and finitely many local derivative bounds.” On a noncompact source, strong/Whitney neighbourhoods may impose locally finite, pointwise conditions everywhere; for example, a positive error bound decaying along R cannot be represented by conditions on finitely many compact sets. The finite-stage reduction therefore does not cover the arbitrary neighbourhood U in the statement.

Step 1.1 says that a transverse map furnished by [L2] is “again a section” because it can be chosen in a neighbourhood of s inside the space of sections. But the cited strong theorem concludes only that every neighbourhood in the space of smooth maps M→E contains a transverse smooth map; it has no constraint pi∘g=id_M. The section condition is not open in that mapping space, so [L2] does not license the conclusion.
